name: Power from water
summary: A small stream with a good drop runs day and night, which beats solar on short winter days. Power in watts is roughly 5 × drop in metres × flow in litres per second, so drop matters most. Pipe water down from upstream onto a wheel driving a treadmill motor or car alternator, or run a centrifugal pump backwards as a turbine.

parts.why: Permanent-magnet motors make simple hydro generators
Car alternators suit fast, high-drop turbines
Pipe that carries water down to the turbine
Centrifugal pumps run backwards as turbines
Carries the wheel or runner shaft
Gears a slow wheel up to generator speed
A diversion controller protects the battery

tips: Measure flow with a bucket and a watch: litres filled ÷ seconds.
A stream falling 10 m at 5 litres per second gives about 250W.
Screen the intake, and never take all of the stream.
Floods wreck riverside gear. Mount the generator well above high water.
